title: Making music on a computer
examples: What is the difference between a DAW and a simple recording app?
Can I record my voice directly into a DAW?
How do I make a beat sound professional in a DAW?

explain.say: Today we are learning about making music using a computer.
A DAW is software that lets you record and edit sound.
Beats are rhythmic patterns of drums and percussion sounds.
Loops are short sections of audio that repeat rhythmically.
Mixing involves balancing all the different sounds together.
In real life, DJs use these concepts to create music sets.

faq.q: What is MIDI data, and is it the same as audio?
faq.a: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface. It records performance data, like which key was pressed and how hard. It is not the actual sound recording itself.
asks: What is the difference between MIDI and audio files?

faq.q: Do I need special equipment to start making music on a computer?
faq.a: While it helps, you can start with just the software. A microphone or MIDI keyboard will help you record better sounds.
asks: What hardware do I need for music production?

faq.q: How do I make a loop sound natural, not repetitive?
faq.a: You can change the tempo or slightly alter the pitch of the loop. This makes it feel like it's evolving.
asks: Can I change the speed of a loop?

faq.q: What is the main goal when mixing music?
faq.a: The main goal is to make sure every sound can be heard clearly without any one sound overpowering the others. It is about balance.
asks: How do I make my music sound good?

faq.q: Can I use a DAW to record live instruments?
faq.a: Yes, if you connect the instrument to an audio interface, the DAW can record the electrical signal. This captures the real sound.
asks: Can I record guitar into the computer?
What do I connect my instrument to?

facts: DAWs allow users to record, edit, and mix digital audio.
MIDI data records performance information, not the actual sound wave.
Beats are built from rhythmic patterns of percussion sounds.
Mixing involves adjusting the volume and balance of different tracks.

quiz.say: A DAW is best described as:
quiz.show: A DAW is best described as:

options.show: Software for recording and editing sound
options.say: Software for recording and editing sound

quiz.why: This is correct because a DAW is a digital application designed for all stages of audio production.

wrong.0: A physical desk is hardware, but a DAW is the software program you run on the computer.
wrong.1: A microphone only captures sound; it cannot edit or arrange multiple tracks.
wrong.2: A textbook teaches concepts, but it does not allow you to manipulate actual audio files.

quiz.say: If you want to repeat a four-beat drum pattern, what musical element are you creating?
quiz.why: A loop is specifically defined as a short section of audio that is designed to repeat.

wrong.0: Mixing is the process of balancing sounds, not creating a repeating section.
wrong.1: The DAW is the overall workspace; the loop is a specific component within it.
wrong.3: A beat is the pattern itself, but a loop is the act of repeating that pattern.

quiz.say: When balancing vocals and bass, you are primarily adjusting:
quiz.why: Mixing fundamentally relies on adjusting the relative volume, or level, of each sound source.

wrong.0: Rhythm is about timing; volume is about perceived loudness.
wrong.2: Tempo affects the speed of the music, not the balance between two specific sounds.
wrong.3: Key signature relates to musical harmony, not the loudness balance of different instruments.
